tagline.text: A broad, multi-tiered waterfall deep in Calbayog's jungle on Samar

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May, relatively dry (the later rainy months are popular too, when the water is high)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day to a full day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,000 (per person, from Calbayog city center)

children.text: Tarangban Falls is a multi-tiered waterfall deep in the jungle of Barangay Tinaplacan, Calbayog City, on Samar Island. After arranging a guide and a motorcycle at the registration post, a walk of about 30 minutes brings you to water spreading wide over the rocks and cold swimming pools.

Tarangban Falls lies in Calbayog City on the western side of Samar Island in Eastern Visayas, Philippines. Calbayog is nicknamed the "City of Waterfalls," and Tarangban is described as one of the tallest and largest falls in the city. I could not find a measured height from a reliable source, so think of the falls less in terms of a number and more as water fanning out widely down several rock steps. It is reached from Barangay Tinaplacan, off the national highway running north from Calbayog toward Allen, and many visitors combine it with Bangon Falls, which starts from the same village.

Vehicles cannot reach the falls, so the routine is to register at the post beside the highway, get a guide assigned, ride a motorcycle (habal-habal) to the trailhead, and then climb on foot. Reviews put the walk at about
20–40 minutes

, and it depends on your pace and the weather because the route mixes forest paths, steps and wet rock. On Google Maps the falls carry more than 90 reviews with a rating in the high 4s, so visitors are clearly happy with the trip.
The atmosphere is quiet. Some reviewers who arrived early had the falls almost to themselves, while others note that crowds build from around
on weekend mornings. There is almost no lodging or restaurant near the falls, so the usual plan is to stay in Calbayog and make a day trip.

Fees and transport details differ from blog to blog and review to review. This guide gives the range that several sources share, and where I could not confirm an official rate it says to check locally. Before you go, ask the Calbayog city tourism office or the registration post about current fees and whether the site is open.

blocks.title: A wide fall in several tiers

children.text: The water does not drop in a single ribbon. It spreads across several slanted rocks in a wide curtain. Up close it is overwhelming, and many reviewers say it is hard to fit into one photo.

blocks.title: Cold pools and a natural massage

children.text: There are swimmable pools below and above the falls, and the water is cold. Standing under the stream lets the water pound your shoulders like a natural massage, but on days when the current is strong you should follow your guide's instructions.
The path climbs through coconut trees, ferns and jungle. One review mentions a paved section of more than 500 steps, and the dirt trail turns slippery after rain.
A guide is assigned at the registration post and points out dangerous sections and crossing points when the water is high. For first-time visitors, going with a guide is close to a necessity.
Bangon Falls starts from the same Barangay Tinaplacan and is close, so you can see both in one day. The common order is to climb Tarangban first and stop at Bangon on the way down.
Go early and there are few people, with only the sounds of water and forest. Reports say mobile signal is almost nonexistent, which makes it a good place for a digital detox.

items.title: Tarangban at a relaxed pace
items.subtitle: Spend more time at the falls with a guide

children.text: Taking a taxi or tricycle all the way to the Tinaplacan registration post saves time, but fares vary widely between reviews. Haggle and agree on a price first.
Finish registration, get your guide, and set off.
Arrive at the falls. Take your photos first, while few people are around.
Swim, stand under the falls for a massage, and rest on the rocks. If rain starts, get out of the water immediately.
Eat your snacks and lunch, then head down. Wet rocks are slippery, so do not rush.

Flights are reported between Manila and Calbayog Airport (CYP). A new terminal and extended runway opened in May 2021, so aircraft as large as the Airbus A320 can now operate there. Routes and schedules change from season to season, however, so check directly with Philippine Airlines (PAL) and Cebu Pacific.
You can also connect through Cebu. Cebgo flies from Mactan, Cebu to Calbayog.

items.title: From the post to the trailhead

children.text: From the registration post, a habal-habal (motorcycle taxi) takes you to the trailhead. Reviews put the fare at
. One blog reported
for 1 to 3 people.
From the trailhead you climb to the falls on foot.

Tarangban changes a great deal with how much water it carries. One reviewer wrote that the falls are most impressive in the rainy season, but at that time the forest trail turns to mud and the rocks become slippery, which raises the risk.

It rains on Samar throughout the year, so a clear day is never guaranteed. Going between December and May, the months generally considered drier, usually means a better trail, but December can still bring rain from typhoons and the northeast monsoon. In any month, check the Calbayog weather and the condition of the falls locally the day before you go.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Water is high early in the period, and it is cool. Watch out for sudden rain.
Comfortable for trekking and good for swimming. The flow may drop.
The most water, but the forest trail is dangerous. Entry may be restricted when it rains.

and may vary depending on local conditions.
There is almost no lodging near the falls, so most people stay in Calbayog city. Downtown has several hotels and guesthouses, and the airport is described as about
10 minutes
from town by car. The falls are around
1 hour
from Calbayog by public transport, so it is best to stay at least a night and make the trip from there.

Food at the falls is limited to drinks and simple snacks at the village store. One reviewer found no eatery near the registration post, so eat a hearty breakfast in town and bring water and snacks. Have dinner at a restaurant in Calbayog.
Start early. Go early and you may have the falls almost to yourself and avoid both the heat and the crowds.
Reviewers say the last jeepney leaves around
, so finish your descent by
at the latest.
Wear trekking shoes with good grip or sandals with straps. One reviewer found flip-flops slippery.
Mobile signal may be unavailable, so charge your phone before leaving and bring a waterproof pouch.
Bring swimwear, a change of clothes, mosquito repellent and sunscreen. Reviewers say there is little space to change.
Carry plenty of small bills. Guide and habal-habal fees are paid in cash.
Do not use soap, shampoo or detergent at the falls. Take your trash back with you.
Watch out for fallen coconuts on the road during the habal-habal ride and on the walk.
If rain starts, get out of the water at once. When the water rises upstream, the current becomes fast and dangerous.
Wet rock is very slippery. A reviewer reported a fall, so move slowly and follow your guide.
Fees differ from review to review, and some visitors say they were asked for extra payment for guiding or photo stops. Confirm the price before you set out.
If you miss the last ride back, you may have no easy way home. Line up a habal-habal or taxi in advance.
Reviewers mention many mosquitoes on the forest trail, so apply repellent and wear long clothing.
Garbage at the foot of the falls has also been raised as a problem. Do not leave anything behind and take your trash back with you.
A fall in the same Barangay Tinaplacan. It is easier to reach than Tarangban and has a swimmable pool below. Most visitors stop here on the way down from Tarangban.
A canyon pool said to be in the same area. It has no signpost, so going with a guide is safer. You must make a steep descent.

blocks.title: Calbayog city center and Maguinoo Port

children.text: The city center, with lodging and restaurants, is about
10 minutes
by car from the airport. Boats to Cebu also leave from here.
About
1 hour
north of Calbayog by jeepney, Allen is the hub for ferries toward Matnog on Luzon. You pass through it when leaving Samar to the north.
